text.p: French engineering and telecommunications group Alcatel Alsthom is interested in the privatisation announced on Wednesday night of Thomson-CSF, the defence electronics subsidiary of Thomson SA, but is waiting to see the terms, an Alcatel spokesman said on Thursday.
"We were interested in Thomson-CSF before and, a priori, we're still interested, but we're waiting to see the terms" before deciding whether to make an offer, he told Reuters.
The government said on Wednesday that it would relaunch the privatisation of Thomson that was halted last week, initially with the sale of Thomson-CSF, 58-percent held by Thomson.
The Alcatel spokesman said that, as he understood the statement issued by the finance ministry, the only privatisation currently under way was that of the Thomson-CSF unit.
He had no comment on Thomson Multimedia (TMM), Thomson's wholly-owned consumer electronics operation.
The ministry said TMM would need a recapitalisation before being privatised and did not give a timetable but said it hoped to privatisate Thomson-CSF in the early months of 1997.

The government, which previously sought to sell the company as a whole, halted that operation last week after the independent Privatisation Commission objected to the terms of the proposed sale of TMM to Korea's Daewoo Electronics .
The government in October said it preferred the offer for Thomson submitted by Lagardere Groupe over Alcatel's bid, but the commission leaned in favour of Alcatel's proposal.
Lagardere would have acquired Thomson for one franc following a state recapitalisation and would have sold TMM to Daewoo, also for one franc.
Alcatel also bid for the entire group and said it would not have sold control of TMM.
